National Consumer Disputes Redressal
H.G. Jain vs Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd. & 2 Ors. on 14 July, 2025
NATIONAL CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
 NEW DELHI
 CONSUMER COMPLAINT NO. NC/CC/284/2015

H.G. JAIN
PRESENT ADDRESS - S/o. Sh. Gautamchand Jain, R/o. Dhavaldhara, Girnar Complex, Adalat
Road, , Aurangabad.
 .......Complainant(s)

 Versus

VOLKSWAGEN INDIA PVT. LTD. & 2 ORS.
PRESENT ADDRESS - Having Its Office at P.O. Box 1849, D-38436 Wolfsburg , Germany
Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd.
PRESENT ADDRESS - E-1, MIDC Industrial Area Phase-III Village Nigoje Mhalunge
kharabawadi, Chakan Tal Khed, , Pune - 410 501 , Maharashtra ,
Volkswagen Group Sales India Pvt. Ltd.
PRESENT ADDRESS - Silver Utopia, 3rd & 4th Floor, Cardinal Gracious Road, Chakala, Andheri
East, , Mumbai - 400 099. , Maharashtra. ,
B.U. Bhandari Automotive Pvt. Ltd.
PRESENT ADDRESS - A-3, Abhimanshree Society, Pashan Road, Pashan, , Pune -411 008
 .......Opposite Party(s)

BEFORE:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE A. P. SAHI , PRESIDENT
 HON'BLE MR. BHARATKUMAR PANDYA , MEMBER

FOR THE COMPLAINANT:
 MR. PRASOUK JAIN, ADVOCATE MR. ANURAG SHARMA, ADVOCATE

FOR THE OPPOSITE PARTY:
 MS. EKTA BHASIN, ADVOCATE MR. SANIDHYA SONTHALIA, ADVOCATE FOR OP-
 1 MR. R. GOPALAKRISHNAN, ADVOCATE FOR OP-2

DATED: 14/07/2025
 ORDER
A.P. Sahi, J. (President)
1. This Complaint arises out of an allegation of deficiency in service against the Opposite

Parties regarding the defects in a luxury car purchased by the Complainant manufactured by

Volkswagen and purchased by the Complainant from the dealer M/s B. U. Bhandari Automotive
 Pvt. Ltd. Opposite Party No. 3 herein. The Complaint was filed on 17.04.2015 in which notices

were issued on 01.05.2015. The Complaint originally designed had four Opposite Parties namely
1. Volkswagen A.G. (Volkswagen Aktiengesellschaft); 2. Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd.; 3.

Volkswagen Group Sales India Pvt. Ltd. and 4. B. U. Bhandari Automotive Pvt. Ltd. The original

Opposite Party No. 1 situated at Germany was sought to be served through the Ministry of Law

and Justice. This exercise of service continued for long and ultimately the Complainant moved an

Application for deleting the Opposite Party No. 1 through IA/1194/2022 that was allowed on

17.02.2022. Consequently, Opposite Party No. 1 was struck off from the array of parties.
2. Of the remaining three, the original Opposite Party No. 2 and 3, now Opposite Party No. 1

and 2 were served but in spite of service of notice they failed to file their written version within time

and consequently their right to file a written version was rejected on 14.10.2015. RA/275/2015 was

filed seeking review of the said Order which was also rejected on 14.12.2015. The said Opposite

Parties approached the Apex Court by filing special leave to Appeal No. 35031 of 2015 that was

dismissed on 04.01.2016. Consequently, the said Opposite Parties had their right to file written

version forfeited but they have appeared through their counsel and who have advanced their

arguments in support of the legal contentions raised by them.
3. The present Opposite Parties No. 1 and 2 underwent a legal change of entity under a

scheme approved by the NCLT Mumbai vide Order dated 05.09.2019. A copy of the said Order

was placed on record through IA No. 17119 of 2024 filed on 27.11.2024 vide a Diary No. 39044.

The said Application has been allowed on 02.12.2024 by us whereafter the orders were reserved.

Consequently, with a change of entity as above the amended Memo has been filed and the same

is on record. According to the amended Memo the dealer is now the Opposite Party No. 3. It may

be pointed out that the dealer who was originally the Opposite Party No. 4 has filed his reply on

02.02.2016 vide Diary No. 5064. The said reply is the only written version which is on record

regarding the allegations made in the Complaint. Since that is the only reply on Record, the same

has been taken into consideration along with the documents filed along with the said reply. A reply

was filed to the said response and the matter has been heard accordingly.
4. The grievance of the Complainant is that from the date of purchase the Complainant was

disappointed by the performance of the vehicle which is a product named "Phaeton". The

Complainant alleges that the said version of the vehicle that were produced very few in number

were claimed by the manufacturers to be of the same level of cars as Bentley of England and such

other luxury cars. The vehicle was purchased on 27.4.2011 for a sum of Rs.90,80,592/- inclusive

of insurance and registration charges. The price of the vehicle was Rs.74,53,205/- and an

extended warranty of two years was also purchased by the Complainant for a sum of Rs.87,725/-.
5. According to the Complainant the Vehicle was offered along with an additional attraction of a

complementary Volkswagen "Beetle" car on purchase of the "Phaeton". The Complainant was not

interested in the second car and therefore, he was offered a credit note of Rs.31,61,250/-.
6. With the aforesaid attractions given by the company the Complainant was expecting a high

level of performance but even the basic features like navigation, Bluetooth connectivity and other

components were faulty and were not functioning. The windscreen cracked in April 2014 and by

this time the vehicle had covered only Rs.17,125 Kilometers. According to the Complainant trouble

began with the vehicle on 15.07.2014, when the car started making loud noises on its own that

lasted for about two to three hours. The Complainant was informed of the said occurrence by a

security guard in the morning, and when an attempt was made to open the door of the car the

same would not open and it was observed that the key had a green light on it instead of the usual

red light.
7. On information been sent to the Opposite Party No. 3 in Pune the Complainant was

informed that the engineer would be send from the Aurangabad dealers to inspect the car, who

arrived but was unable to understand the problem and after taking instructions from the dealer, the

door was ultimately opened, but the engineer was unable to start the engine of the vehicle.

According to the engineer the battery had gone dead which in spite of efforts could not get

charged through a portable charger and on 16.07.2014, after a towing vehicle arrived, the

engineer attempted to shift the gears of the car which he could not do. According to the
 Complainant instructions were received from the dealer and then the gears could be shifted but

thereafter the steering wheel would not move and the vehicle could not roll to align it with the

towing vehicle.
8. The vehicle could not be taken away and then again an attempt was made to get back with

a charged battery and after three days on 19.07.2014 an attempt was made to start the vehicle

which upon being started cranked. According to the Complainant it was the same noise which had

occurred on the first day. Ultimately an engineer from Pune, some Mr. John, came along with the

Aurangabad engineer on 20.07.2014 and after inspection he informed the Complainant about

water having entered and filled under the foot mat of the passenger side of the car, that might

have possibly damaged the ECM unit located there. The engineer apprehended that might be the

probable cause for the malfunctioning. The Complainant alleges that this was news to him as the

car had neither been driven in a water logged area nor affected by water in any way. A towing

vehicle was arranged after 20 days thereafter and on 09.08.2014 the car was towed to Pune

whereafter it was confirmed that the ECM unit under the passenger Compartment of the car was

damaged due to water entry and needed to be replaced. Since the same was to be imported, it

would take a month's time for the same.
9. According to the Complainant he was further informed of the damage of the ECMs in the

other areas of the cars but there was no final solution in sight and therefore, a mail was dispatched

to the manufacturers on 10.09.2014. The said letter is of some significance and therefore is

extracted hereinunder:-
The Complainant alleges that he received the response on 16.09.2014 that the same would

be looked into but of no avail and later on after considerable lapse of time the Complainant was

intimated that the repair of the vehicle would cost about Rs.5,00,000/-. There was no diagnosis of

as to the cause of the water leakage and as such the Complainant on his enquiry after going

through different articles published came to know that there was a manufacturing defect in the
 vehicles manufactured by the Opposite Parties being leakages from the sun roof, AC Pollen filters,

front cowl etc. The articles were communicated to the Opposite Parties by the Complainants and

after having received the same a discount of 65% on spare parts and labour charge was

communicated. The same is extracted hererinunder:-
"Dear Mr Jain

 Greetings from Volkswagen Pune West.
This has reference to your discussion with Mr. Abhijeet Bartakke regarding
 your Vehicle Phaeton

 As discussed, there is an apprehension regarding the Insurance claim not
 being settled by your SBI Insurance company if you opt for reopening the
 previous claim.
Considering this, for your conveniences we will extend our support in terms of
 discount and will offer you 65% discount as a gesture of Goodwill as a
 very special case on the parts & labour charge if you opt to carry out the
 job on paid basis.
As per estimate the total amount is Rs.486634/-out of which your share
 will be only Rs.180135/-
You are requested to send the approval so that we can start working on the
 vehicle and make roadworthy at the earliest

 Please feel free to contact undersigned on 9822871287 in case of query.
Thanking and assuring you our best service support all the time.
With regards

 Hrishikesh Purandare"
10. The aforesaid communications began on 20.10.2014 and on 03.11.2014 the Complainant

was informed that the claim of insurance has been rejected as such 50% discount on the total

repair cost as a measure of goodwill would be offered. The said mail however stated that there

was no manufacturing defect in the car but the cause for entry of water may have given rise to the

problem. On 04.11.2014, the Complainant responded to it by again making a request to the
 Customer Care Officer requesting him to let the Complainant know as to how the water entered in

the front passenger area. The trailing mail dated 04.11.2014 from the Opposite Party confirmed

that there is some external source of water entry while the car was in the premises which was not

known to them. It is after this exchange of communications that the aforesaid offer of 65%

discount was made.
11. The Complainant also alleged that for similar defects a settlement was arrived at by the

manufacturers in respect of other vehicles which were recalled and a suit was also decided

imposing liabilities. These problems were dealt with in the United States in the year 2006 onwards.

What appears is that the Opposite Parties sold the vehicle to the Complainant that appeared to be

an old stock having those defects which could not be sold in the other parts of the world and was

dumped in India. Several notices were sent but with no response and were returned or refused.
12. An invoice of Rs.4,85,738/- was raised for repairs on 03.12.2014. The vehicle was taken by

the Complainant, but on 01.01.2015 the Complainant again found water accumulated inside the

vehicle on the paper foot mat kept in front. The Complainant dispatched this information to the

after sales service and the dealer and also sent pictures of the same. The same was

acknowledged by the Opposite Parties and the car was again sent for repairs to the workshop on

03.01.2015, whereafter it was returned back on 13.01.2015 stating that the issue had been

resolved. There was an advice for getting the beads of the sky roof changed in future.
13. According to the Complainant when he had insisted for a replacement then he was offered a

three segment lower vehicle Jetta as a result thereafter a legal notice was sent once again. The

same was replied from Germany stating that no such car is now being manufactured in India and

therefore the matter should be taken with the Company in India itself. It is with these allegations

that the present Complaint came to be filed.
14. As noted above it was only the dealer who has filed the reply and is on record. There is a

denial of all the allegations with a clear indication that there was no manufacturing defect nor was

there any deficiency in service and hence the Complainant had no case.
15. IA No. 4636 of 2022 was moved on 25.05.2022 through Diary No. 14339 on behalf of the

Complainant seeking permission to bring on record the copy of the owner's manual and the

Registration Certificate. In support of the contention that the vehicle sold to the Complainant was

of an old stock. This was objected to by the Opposite Parties but the said Application was

accepted vide Order dated 18.09.2023. On 22.04.2024 the matter was heard and the following

Order was passed.
"Heard learned Counsel for the Complainant.
Two primary arguments that have been advanced earlier have been
 elaborated by the Complainant. In order to substantiate the first issue with
 regard to the year of manufacturing of the vehicle Volkswagen Phaeton,
 learned Counsel contends that the description given in the Registration
 Certificate on the purchase of the vehicle in the year 2011 demonstrates as if
 the vehicle was manufactured in April, 2011 and purchased by the
 Complainant in April, 2011 whereas according to the Complainant the owner's
 manual of the vehicle that was provided by the
 Opposite Party at the time of the purchase of the vehicle demonstrates that
 the print status of the said document is of the year 2009 and it bears the
 identification number of the vehicle which matches with the Registration
 documents. The contention is that if the owner's manual contains the same
 identification number and has been printed in the year 2009 then in that event
 the vehicle cannot be presumed to have been manufactured in the year 2011
 and consequently the submission is that this amounts to an unfair trade
 practice.
The second ground which is urged is with regard to the deficiency as
 alleged having caused to the vehicle which became subject matter of
 communication between the Complainant and the concerned Opposite Party.
 According to the Complainant it demonstrates that the Opposite Parties even
 though deny a manufacturing defect in the case, yet they themselves have
 identified that there have been repeated concerns of water leakage in the
 vehicle which was identified by them and was also repaired. The submission
 therefore is that the said communications together with Paragraph 9.38 of the
 Written Statement filed by Opposite Party No.-4 acknowledges the entry of
 water inside the passenger cabin possibly from the sun roof because of
 accumulation of dust resulting in blockage of water drainage channel.
The contention is that the repairs which were carried out were because
 of the defects in the car and which was repeated again as is evident from the
 communications and the vehicle on that count had to be repaired twice. The
 submission therefore is that these facts according to the Complainant indicate
 the deficiencies for which learned Counsel for the Complainant has urged that
 such manufacturing complaints were contested by the Opposite Party No.-1 in
 a law suit in 2004-05 in U.S.A. for which an Article published in 2014 as
 Annexure C-7 has been cited to contend that such defects are not unknown
 and therefore the same also should be taken into account for the purpose of
 adjudicating this controversy.
It is the aforesaid the two broad issues that have been urged by the
 learned Counsel for the Complainant to contend that having purchased a
 super luxury car of this high-end from the manufacturers, the least what was
 expected is that the service of the vehicle could have been far better as
 expected, but the Opposite Parties themselves having found these defects
 and are therefore liable to pay damages as claimed.
Learned Counsel for the Opposite Parties have not yet commenced
 their arguments. They pray that the matter be taken up on 06.08.2024 at
 02.00 p.m.
 Learned Counsel for the Opposite Party No.2-3 have handed over the
 Written Submissions to the learned Counsel for the Complainant today."
16. The Complainants have filed the written submissions and a copy thereof was handed over to

the learned Counsel for the Opposite Parties. The written submission alleges unfair trade practice

for misrepresenting and selling a 2009 manufactured car as a 2011 model to the Complainant. It is

also alleged that the vehicle was suffering from inherent manufacturing defects which stands

substantiated with similar issues having arisen in all the vehicles manufactured by them globally. It

is also submitted that no expert evidence was required when the facts clearly demonstrated

manufacturing defects with the repeated visit of the vehicle to the Respondents. The Opposite

Parties having failed to rectify the same in spite of having admitted the defects, the deficiency

stands proved and their services were negligent and incompetent. Several decisions have also

been cited in the written submissions and it is in this background that the matter was heard and

Orders were reserved.
17. The evidence affidavits reflect the same arguments as contained in the pleadings. It would

be apt to point out to the first argument of the Complainant regarding the car being of an old stock.

For this learned Counsel has relied on the owner's manual that was printed on 07.09.2009.

Learned Counsel submits that the printing of the owner's manual and the date referred to therein

matches with the identification number mentioned therein. It is urged that the vehicle was sold on

27.04.2011 and registered on 04.05.2011. The submission is that the printing of the manual

establishes that the vehicle was manufactured in 2009 and accordingly the vehicle was

manufactured in all probability in 2009-10.
18. Having perused the records and having considered the submissions including the Written

Submissions, it would be appropriate to deal with the contention raised by the Complainant in Para

9.46 of the Complaint regarding the vehicle being sold to the Complainant out of an old stock. It is

for the said purpose that IA/4636/2022 was moved on behalf of the Complainant alleging that the

documents sought to be brought on record establish the grievance that has already been raised in

the Complaint. The documents were sought to support the said contentions. Orders were passed

on 18.09.2023 accepting the same subject to any objections being raised by the other side. It may

be pointed out that there is no denial of the said documents even though the contents thereof have

been explained by the Opposite Parties to urge that the said documents do not in any way

establish the contention raised on this ground. We have examined the contents of IA/4636/2022

and Paragraph Nos.3 to 7 are extracted herein under:-
3. That the Complainant in the complaint had specifically sought the details of the
 manufacturing year of the vehicle in question from the Opposite Parties as the Complainant
 was under an apprehension that the vehicle sold to him formed a part of the old stock while
 being represented otherwise, however, the Opposite Parties have failed to provide any
 substantial answer to the Complainant and have been proceeded ex- parte in the matter.
4. That while going through the documents received with the vehicle and the
 case file, the Complainant came across the owner's manual which was received along
 with the vehicle. To the utter shock and despair of the Complainant, a perusal of the said
 owner's manual revealed that it was printed on 07.09.2009. That it also mentioned the
 Vehicle Identification Number of the vehicle which can only be obtained after the vehicle is
 manufactured. The details printed on the owner's manual are being reproduced herein for
 the ready reference of this Hon'ble Commission:
Owner's manual:
Phaeton

 Print status: 07.09.2009

 Englisch: 12.2009

 Art-Nr: 103.5R1.PHA.20

 Fzg-Ident-Nr.: WVWZZZ3DZA8004235
 A copy of the owner's manual is annexed herewith as Annexure C-16.
5. The Registration Certificate of the vehicle shows the date of manufacturing to be
 04/2011. It is humbly submitted that the owner's manual being printed in 09/2009 could
 not have had the Vehicle Identification Number printed on it which could not have
 been generated uptil 04/2011.
A copy of the registration certificate of the vehicle is annexed herewith as Annexure
 C-17.
6. Further, the tenth character of the Vehicle Identification Number reveals the year
 of manufacturing and A being the 10th character of the Vehicle Identification Number
 shows that the said vehicle was manufactured in 2010.
7. That the owner's manual shows the date of manufacture as 2009, Vehicle
 Identification Numbers shows it to be 2010 and Registration Certificate shows it to be
 2011. Thus, the owner's manual and the registration certificate of the vehicle are necessary
 to be placed on record for effective adjudication of the matter as the same would aid in
 unveiling the unfair trade practices being adopted by the Opposite Parties.
19. Such an issue on facts was dealt with in the case of
Praveen Kumar Mittal Vs. Porsche

India Pvt. Ltd. CC/55/2018
decided on 24.04.2023 that has been relied on by the learned

Counsel for the Complainant in his Written Arguments. In that case, there were two sets of

documents placed, one by the Complainant and one by the Opposite Party. It was found on facts

that one of the sets produced by the Opposite Party could not be accepted as it appeared to be

manipulated.
20. In the instant case, there is no such dispute. There is only one set of documents produced

by the Complainant. The Owner's Manual describes its status of print as 07.09.2009 and it bears

the Vehicle Identification Number as WVWZZZ3DZA8004235. The said document is Annexure C-

16 and is followed by Annexure C-17, which is the Registration Certificate of the vehicle bearing
 Registration Number MH20 CA 8910. The date of manufacture is mentioned as 04/2011. The

date of Registration is 04.05.2011 and the Registration is valid till 03.05.2026. The vehicle is

registered in the name of Mr.Harshwardhan Jain and it bears Chassis (CH) No.

WVWZZZ3DZA8004235.
21. The Vehicle Identification Number mentioned on the Owner's Manual is the same as the

Chassis Number mentioned in the Registration Certificate. The Complainant in IA No.4636/2022

quoted above has come out with a case that the vehicle in all possibility/ probability was

manufactured in 2009 or 2010. We are inclined to accept this argument inasmuch as the vehicle

came to be sold on 27.04.2011 and was registered on 04.05.2011. There is nothing in the

Affidavit of the dealer to demonstrate, that the vehicle was manufactured in 2011. The

Complainant in Paragraph 9.46 has made allegations of the car being of an old stock.
22. The reply given by the dealer is a bald denial but it is stated that the vehicle had been used

for more than four years by the time the Complaint was filed. The explanation given is that it was

a right hand driven vehicle manufactured for countries like India, and had it been a vehicle for the

United States it would have been a left hand drive. It is on this basis, it was contended that the

vehicle was in no way of an old stock meant to be marketed in the US or any other country. On

the demand of the documents pertaining to manufacturing in Paragraph 9.47 of the Complaint, the

reply given by the dealer is that the demand is baseless and all relevant documents pertaining to

the vehicle were available with the Complainant. Reliance has been placed on the year of

manufacture mentioned in the Registration Certificate that was in the possession of the

Complainant since 2011.
23. Having considered the said pleadings and documents on record, we find that the Owner's

Manual may have been printed in 2009 and the vehicle may have been, during the process of

manufacture, been identified with the Chassis Number. Admittedly, these vehicles were very few

in number and possibly the Owner's Manual might have been printed with the Chassis Number

while the vehicle was still being assembled for being sold and delivered thereafter. The vehicle

being a right hand drive model cannot be possibly a manufacture for customers in the US where

left hand drive is the rule. The speculation by the Complainant that when the vehicle failed

survival in the American market, was then dumped in India, is simply imaginary and based on no
 material.
24. Nonetheless the vehicle must have been manufactured prior to 27.04.2011, which is the

date of purchase by the Complainant and it is quite possible that the vehicle might have been

completely assembled for being delivered in 2010 as stated by the Complainant himself as per its

VIN.
25. However, the allegation of deficiency that an old stock was sold to the Complainant may not

be an acceptable argument for other pragmatic reasons. The Complaint was instituted on

17.04.2015, which is approximately four years after the purchase of the vehicle. The Complainant

in Paragraph 9.47 of the Complaint has demanded the date of manufacture and the date of

shipping of the vehicle from the Germany to India and has then supported his contentions with the

Owner's Manual and the Registration Certificate filed along with IA/4636/2022. What is interesting

is that this Application and Affidavit was filed after seven years of the filing of the Complaint on

25.05.2022. Not only this, Paragraph 4 of the Application as extracted hereinabove reveals that

the Complainant came across the Owner's Manual that was "received along with the vehicle". It is

well known that admission is the best piece of evidence. The Complainant having admitted to

have received the Owner's Manual on 27.04.2011, which is the date of purchase, it is established

that the Complainant was aware of the contents of the Owner's Manual, which refers to the date of

print as well as the Vehicle Identification Number that is identical to the Chassis Number

mentioned in the Registration Certificate. The averment in IA No.4636/2022 that this was to the

utter shock and surprise of the Complainant is, therefore, incorrect. The information contained in

the Owner's Manual and the Registration Certificate was available to the Complainant on the date

of purchase in 2011 according to his own admission. The averments made in Paragraph 9.46 and

9.47, therefore, do not inspire any creditworthiness as these averments made after four years of

the purchase of the vehicle when the Complaint was filed do not reconcile with the candid

admission made in Para 4 of IA No.4636 of 2022.
26. Additionally the issue is sought to be substantiated by bringing forth the documents after

seven years of the filing of the Complaint in 2022. Thus, the Complainant is attempting this

argument after eleven years of the purchase of the vehicle before this Commission inspite of the

fact that the Owner's Manual and the Registration Certificate was available to him in 2011itself.
27. A suspicion was cast by the Complainant in the Legal Notice dispatched on 25.11.2014 in

Paragraph 41, but the same was without any foundation. While giving the second Notice on

29.01.2015, the Complainant addressed the same to the present Opposite Parties where there is

no allegation about an old stock but in Paragraph 15 it has been put differently that the said

vehicle was sold in Indian market after changing their VIN Number as it could not be sold

anywhere else and, therefore, the same was a dumping activity of the Company.
28. The aforesaid documents, the contents thereof read with Paragraph 4 of IA/4636/2022 leads

us to believe that this argument has been put forth for an imagery of disreputable business with no

objection having been raised inspite of being possessed of the documents when the vehicle was

purchased in 2011.
29. There is one more additional probable reason that can support the aforesaid conclusion,

namely, that the Complainant with open eyes accepted the alluring offer that was made for the

sale of the vehicle, as, apart from the discounted price, the vehicle was offered along with an

additional attraction of a complimentary Volkswagen Beetle vehicle or in the alternative a Credit

Note of Rs.31,61,250/-.
30. We may point out that most of the time products are sold with added attractions to arouse

interest in prospective customers who are also on the lookout not to miss any bargains to their

liking. Sellers offer deductions and allowances for prospective buyers to prioritize their need in

favour of the seller's product. Such incentives are offered to customers for taking interest which is

to advance sales. This method of an offer to sell products on less than their face value or

customary price is in the ordinary parlance of bargain referred to as a discount offer. The offer of

a Volkswagen Beetle, as buy 1 get one free, was in our opinion not a mere attraction but a

tempting invitation, more or less enticing, when an alternative of a credit note of such a huge

amount accompanied the same. The buyer, more particularly a businessman like the Complainant

ought to have treaded on this path with caution. Caveat Emptor is a well-known principle. The

Complainant therefore cannot term it as a misleading bargain. The purchase of the vehicle was a

conscious decision of the Complainant.
31. The vehicle was, therefore, voluntarily purchased by the Complainant with the aforesaid

incentives acceptable to the Complainant and, therefore, to allege that a vehicle manufactured
 earlier of an old stock was sold to the Complainant does not appear to be a matter of deception or

unfair trading as the Complainant purchased the vehicle together with such huge benefits and also

received the Owner's Manual as explained hereinabove. We are, therefore, not inclined to

entertain this argument or accept the same as an alleged deficiency on the part of the Opposite

Parties, looking to the fact that the Complainant had purchased the vehicle and had received the

Owner's Manual with the entire information regarding the year of manufacture along with the

incentives
referred to above
.
32. Moving to the submissions regarding the defects and deficiencies point out, the allegations

regarding the same have been made about the defects that were reported and the task

undertaken that has been narrated in Paragraph 9.8 to 9.35. It may be pointed out that when the

vehicle had met with the problem of the windscreen having cracked in April, 2014, the same is

stated to have been returned after repairs on 17.05.2014 by which time the vehicle had covered

more than 17,000 kms. as stated in Paragraph 9.11. The said fact of the vehicle having been

delivered in satisfactory condition to the Complainant is evident from the Satisfaction Note dated

17.05.2014 that has been filed by the dealer/ Opposite Party No.3 (previously Opposite Party

No.4) along with his Reply. The said Satisfaction Note is extracted herein under:-
33. The first Complaint raised thereafter is about an incident of 15.07.2014, which is after more

than two years of the purchase of the vehicle. It may be point out that the vehicle had a warranty

of two years and the Complainant had purchased an additional warranty for two years that is on

record. The warranty conditions also indicate that they cover a huge mileage and the additional

warranty was for a further One Lakh Kilometers. Thus, the vehicle had been driven within the

mileage covered under the warranty conditions.
34. The Complainant has narrated as to why the vehicle started giving trouble and a mysterious

failure had occurred as the car started itself at odd hours probably on its own. The failure of ECMs

had been located, which is evident from the information given to the Complainant clarifying the
 same. The Complainant had written directly to the manufactures on 10.09.2014 complaining them

about the mysterious failure of ECMs and draining of the battery as well as the other complaints to

which a reply was given on 16.09.2014 that the same shall be looked into. It was forwarded to the

Brand Manager in India where after vide a mail dated 20.10.2014, the Complainant was offered

the discount of 65% as a goodwill gesture as against spares and labour. The insurance claim of

the Complainant was not accepted and after having received the said information another mail

was received from the Customer Care, Mumbai informing the Complainant that there was no

manufacturing defect but the damage caused to the controls was due to water entry in the

passenger compartment. Thus, the defect having been caused due to a water entry in the

passenger compartment was indicated in this mail dated 03.11.2014. It appears that by this time

the insurance claim was not accepted and the discount earlier offered was reduced to 50% on

03.11.2014. The Complainant sent his response to the same and a trailing mail was received on

04.11.2014 confirming that there is some external source of water entry in the car but at the same

time it was suggested that this might have happened at the end of the Complainant while the

vehicle was in his premises, which was not known to the Opposite Parties.
35. It is also on record that an invoice of Rs.4,85,738/- had been raised for carrying out the

repairs on which the discounts etc. had been offered. The liability to make full payment was,

therefore, reduced with the discount offer as against the said invoice and the vehicle was

thereafter taken back by the Complainant, which is indicated in the Evidence Affidavit of the

Complainant.
36. The Complainant had also demanded the replacement of the vehicle but according to him no

reply was received.
37. It is alleged by the Complainant that the vehicle had been kept for repairs of about 148 days

and on 01.01.2015 the Complainant again found the presence of water inside the vehicle on the

paper foot mat kept in the front foot well. The Complainant also alleges to have dispatched

photographs whereupon the two Engineers were sent to whom the Complainant suggested for

carrying out a shower test. According to the Complainant some leakage was again witnessed that

was relatable to the sunroof of the vehicle. This time the vehicle was again kept for another 10

days and it was informed on 13.01.2015 that the issue had been resolved.
38. The fact about the vehicle having suffered this defect is also evident from the Affidavit of the

dealer, now the Opposite Party No.3. Even though the dealer had alleged that the vehicle had

been kept uncared by the Complainant, and it is quite possible that the water had been allowed to

enter through an open window, but in the Reply to Paragraph No.9.37 and 9.38, the dealer has

admitted as follows:-
"Moreover, the annexures attached by the Complainant are not relevant to the
 present case as there has been an evident entry of water inside the passenger cabin
 from the sun roof because of accumulation of dust which resulted in blockage of
 water drainage channel."
39. The dealer had also stated that that heavy discount had been offered purely as a goodwill. It

is also stated in Paragraph 9.40 of the Reply that the presence of water in the left side front foot

area was noticed and informed to the Complainant. It was, however, denied by the dealer that

there was any manufacturing defect in the ECMs units and that the design of the vehicle along

with his parts stood approved by the Automotive Research Association of India, which is a

Government of India approved body authorized to certify that the car is suitable for Indian

conditions. The aforesaid documents along with repair order card indicates that the leakage of

water had been noticed and is a defect that was attended to by the Opposite Parties. The mail

dated 06.01.2015 sent by the Opposite Parties to the Complainant confirms the same. Even

though the said mail indicates that the rectification is being carried out, the same would be made

known once the vehicle is ready. The mail dated 06.01.2015 is extracted herein under:-
40. It is thereafter that the vehicle was delivered on 13.01.2015 stating that issue had been

resolved.
41. The aforesaid facts therefore, leave no room for doubt that there was a problem of leakage

from the sunroof as a result whereof the water travelled to an area where the ECM was located.

Not only this, the Complainant had been informed that ECMs located elsewhere also had been

affected and required to be replaced. In the given circumstances, it is evident that the ECMs were
 suffering from defects and the same required replacement, which according to the dealer was

carried out and the vehicle was delivered on 13.01.2015. Thus this defect and imperfection

continued this long from 15.07.2014 onwards.
42. The Complainant dispatched a Legal Notice on 29.01.2015 to which a Reply was given on

09.02.2015 that the car was not manufactured in India and, therefore, their claim is being

forwarded to the concerned Company.
43. That thereafter the Complainant again raised an issue that the car was not starting and

somebody by the name of Mr.Purandare of Pune Workshop was contacted. According to whom

there was a minor problem with the batteries. It was also explained that the car would start

intermittently and there was something noticed while depressing the break paddle, which would

help start the car when it was pressed slightly, but if the paddle was depressed completely then

the vehicle could not start. The car was, therefore, once again sent on 25.03.2015 and the

Complainant was again informed about the replacement of batteries. It is in these circumstances

that the Complaint came to filed in April 2015 with the allegations made therein.
44. The question as to whether these persistent defects were manufacturing defects or any

other defect or not. The Complainant has also relied on certain material to indicated that various

models manufactured by the M/s Volkswagen namely Beetle, Zeta, Golf, Passat and Audi A-6

vehicles were suffering with similar defects and were recalled for which reliance has been placed

by the Complainant. Apart from this regarding such defects law suits that were filed for 69 million

dollars were settled by the Volkswagen and the said material was available on the internet with the

heading "Volkswagen settles 69 million dollar law suit over leaking sunroof". The Complainant,

therefore, contends that this leakage was a phenomenon in the vehicles manufactured by

Volkswagen through their range of mode and, therefore, there was every reason to believe that

this was a manufacturing defect that was common to vehicles manufactured by Volkswagen that

gave rise to various contests as reported in the said material filed on record.
45. The question which needs consideration is as to whether the defect of the leaking sunroof

resulting in the damage to the ECMS and then the consequences of the vehicle malfunctioning

amounts to a manufacturing defect or any imperfection or not. No expert evidence has been led by

the Complainant and the complaint has gone uncontroverted on behalf of the Opposite Parties
 No.1 & 2. The Opposite Party No.3 who is the dealer has controverted the allegation of

manufacturing defect and has urged that the claim of the Complainant does not fall within the

scope of a manufacturing defect as alleged and hence the complaint deserves to be dismissed. It

has also been urged that there has been no breach of any warranty and the car has been serviced

and repaired promptly with all available resources and facilities that were needed.
46. It is correct that when such issues arise there may be a requirement of an expert opinion to

ascertain as to whether the sequences of events of leakage of water, the failure of the ECMS and

the consequences arises therefrom can be correlated to a manufacturing defect. If that is so

whether any such expert opinion is warranted in the present case.
47. The question of leakage of water and its possibility of having entered through the sky roof

therefore appears to be highly probable as it is evident from the mails and the affidavit of the

dealer as discussed above. Due to the presence of water, the failure of ECMS is also evident as

the repairs to that effect have been carried out by the dealer. These failures being technical in

nature, had to be explained by the Opposite Parties who could not rely on the written version of

Opposite Parties No.1 & 2 as it was beyond time and the written version filed by the dealer does

not substantiate the same. To the contrary the dealer has accepted the fact of leakage in the

sunroof.
48. While dealing with this issue we may point out that a vehicle need not necessarily have a

manufacturing defect. Even if there is a defect within the warranty period then a liability can arise.

This issue was dealt by this Commission very recently in the case of Kishor N. Shah vs. M/s

Mercedes Benz India Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. - Consumer Complaint No.301 of 2012 where the

earlier judgements on the subject from 2009 onwards were assessed and it was observed as

under:-
"12.2 A bare perusal of the definition of word 'defect' (which is a definition for all kinds of
 goods, which includes the automobiles/cars, under Section 2(1) (d), as reproduced above,
 shows that any kind of 'fault' or 'imperfection' or 'shortcoming' in the 'quality', 'quantity',
 potency', 'purity' or 'standard', which is 'required to be maintained', 'by or under any law' or
 'under any contract', 'express or implied' or 'as claimed by the trader in any manner,
 whatsoever constitutes 'defect'. The Act does not define the term 'manufacturing defect' or
 any other specific kind/type of defect, it only defines 'defect'.
(a) In
Maruti Udyog Limited v. Hasmukh Lakshmichand
, 2009 SCC OnLine NCDRC 74,
 this Commission observed as follows:
"Manufacturing defect" as per P. Ramanatha Aiyar's Advanced Law Lexion, 3RD Edition,
Volume 3, 2005, defines to mean as:-
"An unintended aspect of finished product due to error or omission in assembly or
manufacture, that causes injury."
Business Dictionary.com defines it to mean:-
"Frailty or shortcoming in a product resulting from a departure from its design
specifications during production."
xxxx

The "manufacturing defect" is much more than an ordinary defect which can be cured by
replacing the defective part. Manufacturing defect is fundamental basic defect which
creeps while manufacturing a machinery. To prove such a defect, opinion of an Expert is
necessary...
(b) In
Nuzhat v. Dee Dee Motors Pvt. Ltd. and Another
RP No. 1053/2016, decided
on 03.12.2019, (2019 SCC OnLine NCDRC 1691), this Commission observed:
"Manufacturing defect is a defect which persistently comes up and cannot be rectified
even after attempts made by the dealer. The Oxford English Dictionary, Tenth Edition
(Indian Edition)-definition of defect is as under:
'Shortcoming' imperfection or lack"
(c) In M/s Hyundai Motors Indi Ltd. Vs. M/s Affiliated East West Press (P) Ltd. RP
No. 1053/2016, decided on 03.12.2019, ( 2019 SCC OnLine NCDRC 1691), this
Commission observed:
"In our view, if a brand new car gives trouble within a few days of its purchase, the
consumer would be dissatisfied. .....Further, a person who purchases a vehicle, maybe a
luxury Accent car or a small car, would not be satisfied, if it is a defective vehicle. That the
defect may not be a major one but the consumer loses satisfaction of having a new car.
That loss of satisfaction would be much more in a case when the person buys the vehicle
with his hard-earned money."
(d) In
Anand Kumar Bansal V. Premier Ltd. RP No.
2816/2015 (2019 SCC OnLine
 NCDRC 1048), this Commission observed:
"15. .... Since 'defect' means any imperfection or shortcoming and 'manufacturing defect' is
 a shortcoming in a product resulting from departure from its design and is dangerous than
 the consumer expects the product to be, we are of the considered view that stoppage of
 engine and replacement of the same twice during the first year squarely falls within the
 definition of 'defect' and 'manufacturing defect............."
12.3 Section14 of the Act empowers the commission to allow various reliefs, including
 the replacement of the goods with new goods of the similar description (car in the present
 case), return (refund) of the price paid by the Complainant, award of compensation for any
 loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to negligence of the OP, if the Commission
 comes to a finding that the goods in question suffered from any of the defects specified in
 the complaint or that any of the allegations contained in the complaint about the services
 are proved. Act also empowers the Commission to award punitive damages if the
 circumstances so warrant. Of course, the exact nature of relief from amongst those listed
 u/s 14 of the Act and/or quantum of compensation and punitive damages etc. will depend
 on facts and circumstances of the case.
12.4 Under the provisions of the Act, any good, like the car in the present case, can be
 ordered to be replaced or the cost can be ordered to be refunded if it suffers from any
 'defect' as defined in the Act. It is not necessary that for ordering a replacement of good or
 refund of its cost, the good (car) must suffer from any 'manufacturing defect'. There is no
 such concept of goods suffering from manufacturing defect under the Act, which only
 defines the 'defect'. Of course, even if the defect in a good/car is established, it does not
 necessarily have to result in directions of replacement of good/car or refund of its cost.
 Exact nature of relief to be granted would depend on facts and circumstances of the case.
 Further the provisions of the Act with respect to powers of Commission to order
 replacement of car or refund will have overriding effect over the terms & conditions of the
 warranty.
49. The Commission also went on to deal with the obligations of the seller and further observed

in paragraphs 12.5 to 12.7 as follows:-
"12.5 Whenever a manufacturer/Dealer of a vehicle offers to sell a brand new vehicle to
 the consumer, there is an implied contract as to the claim of the manufacturer/dealer that
 the vehicle being sold does not suffer from and will not suffer from any kind of fault or
 imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency and standard which is
 required to be maintained.
In
Hyundai Motors India Ltd. Vs. Shailendra Bhatnagar
(2022 SCC OnLine SC 482),
 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed "...... Vehicles are goods within the meaning of
Section
 2(7)
of the Sale of Goods Act 1930 and they carry implied conditions as to their fitness.
 That is a statutory mandate and that mandate also operates in respect of goods, whose
 defect is subject of proceedings in a consumer complaint under the
Consumer Protection
 Act
1986....."
12.6 How does a purchaser of a new vehicle, who is neither an expert in automobile
 Engineering, nor expected to be so, perceive a manufacturing defect or a defect in the car?
 Whenever a person purchases a new vehicle, be it a low end vehicle or a middle end
 vehicle or a high end vehicle, depending upon his economic status/affording capacity, has
 great sentimental/emotional values attached to such purchase/acquisition of new vehicle.
 Even an unwanted small scratch or damage to the vehicle in the initial period of such
 purchase upsets not only the purchaser of such vehicle but his family members as well. If
 such a vehicle start giving troubles/manifesting mechanical or other technical issues right
 from the beginning, calling for its repeated visits to the workshop for servicing/repairs etc.,
 such occurrences itself disturbs the peace of mind of such purchaser and cause mental
 agony to him and his family. It is natural for such a Complainant to think that a vehicle
 giving repeated troubles, requiring repeated visits to the workshop, suffers from same kind
 of serious defects, which he tend to classify as 'manufacturing defect', although in all such
 cases, the defects though being there, may not strictly speaking be 'manufacturing defect'.
 In the context of airbags not deployed in an accident, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shailendra
 Bhatnagar (2022) SCC Online SC 483), observed "..... A consumer is not meant to be an
 expert in physics calculating the impact of a collusion of the theories based on velocity and
 force......"
12.7 In cases involves allegations of manufacturing defect in the vehicle, it is typical on
 the part of manufacture and/or dealer to take the plea that the vehicle suffered damage due
 to the negligent handling of the vehicle by the purchaser/complainant and the alleged issues
 are only due to operational/usage reasons, there is lack of proper maintenance etc. The
 standard defence taken by Manufacturers/Dealers in such cases where manufacturing
 defect is alleged and replacement is sought is that vehicle is sold under a warranty for a
 certain specified period from the date of purchase or until vehicle runs for a certain kms.,
 whichever is earlier and that warranty is made subject to certain terms and conditions,
 qualifications and limitations as set out in the warranty booklet and that as per warranty, the
 manufacturers/dealers obligation is limited to repair or replace the defective components at
 its sole discretion during the warranty period if the manufacturer/dealer acknowledge that
 such defect(s) is attributable to faulty material or workmanship at the time of manufacturer."
50. An issue was also raised of the liability of the principal vis-à-vis the dealer. The said issue

was also answered in paragraphs 12.8 and 12.9 as follows:-
"12.8 Further, in cases involving automobiles, it is typical on the part of manufacturer to
plead Principal to Principal relationship rather than Principal to Agent relationship with a
view to avoid its liability for any wrongful acts of their authorized dealer. The issue of
Manufacturer-Dealer relationship came up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in
Tata Motors Ltd. Vs. Antonio Paulo Vaz & Anr. (Civil Appeal No.
574/2021
decided on 18.02.2021). In this case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, after taking note of
dealership agreement, held that the relationship between manufacturer-dealer was that of
Principal to Principal and not that of Principal to Agent. In the present case, the OP-1
(manufacturer) in its pleadings and/or evidence has not specifically claimed either a
Principal to Principal or Principal to Agent relationship with OP-2 (dealer), although during
the hearing the Counsel for OP-1 stated that they work on Principal to Principal basis.
Further, in their submission, OP-1 has taken the plea that there is no privity of contract
between Complainant and OP-1, as admittedly the Complainant purchased the car from
OP-2 and not from OP-1. OP-1 had not provided any services to the Complainant and
hence there is no ground to allege deficiency in services on the part of OP-1. On the
other hand, OP-2 dealer contended during the hearing that notwithstanding that the car in
question has been sold by them, they are concerned with any providing after sale
services and have nothing to do with the defects in the car, in question, if any, contending
further that they have not been deficient in providing any service/after sale service to the
complainant in this case. In a Principal to Agent relationship, the Principal is responsible
for wrong doings of his agent/acts done on behalf of the Principal. However, in a
Principal to Principal relationship, which is generally entered into by car manufacturers
with their. authorized dealers under some kind of a dealership agreement, while the
Principal (Manufacturer) may not be responsible for the wrong doings/acts of negligence
of the Principal (Dealer), it surely is responsible for the warranties it has given with
respect to removing any defects or replacement of parts or replacement of car itself in
case of manufacturing defect(s), as long as conditions of warranties have been
observed/complied with. Although the correspondence between the parties show that
OP-1 and OP-2 were acting in tandem to each other, as if OP-2 was acting like an agent
of OP-1 while conveying various offers like trade in offer, extended warranty etc. on
behalf of OP-1 only, even if it is presumed that relationship between manufacturer and
dealer of a car is' that of Principal to Principal, the manufacturer can only resist/avoid his
responsibility/his liabilities for wrong doings/acts of omissions and commissions of dealer,
but for warranties offered to the customer during the warranty period, and subject
to due compliance of terms of such warranties by the customer, both the
manufacturer and dealer are liable for repairs/replacement of any parts or
replacement of car itself, if the terms of warranty so provide for. Dealer alone
cannot be made to bear the liabilities for repair/replacement of parts and/or
replacement of car on account of manufacturing defect during the warranty period
even in a Principal to Principal relationship.
12.9 In a Principal to Principal relationship, both the manufacturer and authorized
dealer are independent legal entities, dealer buys the car from the manufacturer and then
resells them to customers, the dealer owns the inventory once it is purchased. In a
Principal to Agent relationship, authorized dealer act as an agent of manufacturer, the
dealer sells cars on behalf of the manufacturer in this case, within the scope of authority,
 the manufacturer is liable for the acts of the dealer. In a Principal to Principal
 relationship, although it is the dealer who sells the car, manufacturer can also be held
 liable under the provisions of
Consumer Protection Act
, especially for manufacturing
 defects and product liability clauses. Moreover, the customer/purchasers while
 purchasing a car, never comes into direct contact with the manufacturer and has to buy
 such cars only from an authorized dealer of the manufacturer. No one other than the
 authorized dealer or the manufacturer can sell such car and/or repair/service such cars
 during the warranty period. However, the customer/purchaser goes by the reputation of
 the manufacturer while deciding to buy a particular car based on various features,
 specifications, warrantees etc. advertised by the manufacturer in one way or the other.
 Hence, in our considered view, in in a situation of Principal to Principal relationship, the
 manufacturer of a car cannot escape its liability for a defective car or a car having
 some serious defects.
In
Tata Motors Vs. Pradipta Kundu & Anr. , RP
2133 of 2015
 decided on 02.03.2020, National Commission held that for a defective car, even though
 the car was sold by an authorized dealer, the manufacturer cannot escape liability."
51. The question as to whether an expert opinion is necessary for locating any such defects, the

Commission in paragraph 12.10 has held as under:-
"12.10. As regards requirement or need for a laboratory test/expert opinion to determine
 whether the good/car suffers from any 'defect', in particular a manufacturing defect', a bare
 perusal of provisions of
Section 13(1)(c)
reproduced above shows that such a laboratory
 test and/or expert opinion is required only when 'where the defect in the goods
 cannot be determined without proper analysis or test of goods', it is not mandatory in
 all cases where the complainant alleges a defect in the goods. This Commission has
 taken such a view in many cases.
In M/s.
Kataria Automobiles versus Prabodhkant
 Damodaras Pandya, RP No.
3916 of 2008, decided on 21.09.2021, this Commission
 observed:
"8. In the light of the discussion above, we are of the considered opinion that
 determining 'defect' in accordance with the procedure laid down under
Section 13(1)(c)
to
(g) was not required in this case, and, as such, this "omission", as argued by the learned
 counsel for the Dealer, is not fatal to the case of the Complainant. ................" The Dealer
 received the sale price. It was responsible for satisfactorily repairing the vehicle.
 Determining 'defect' in accordance with the procedure laid down under
Section 13(1)(c)
to
(g) of the Act 1986 was not required in this case. As such there was no need to implead
 the Manufacturer as a necessary party before the District Commission. In any case ........."
In
Hind Motor (I) Ltd. Vs. Lakhbir Singh, RP No.
2790 of 2008 along with RP 4345 of
 2008, decided on 02.12.2013 (2013 SCC OnLine NCDRC 1033), this Commission
 observed:
"19. Furthermore, within eight months of selling of the vehicle, as per petitioners' own
case, it required substantial repairs worth Rs.2.25 lakh. This itself goes on to show that
there were inherent defects in the vehicle, that is, why it required substantial repairs.
Under such circumstances, no expert opinion is required as the facts of the case itself
speaks that major repairs were required just after short span of eight months from the date
of the sale of the vehicle."
In
Tata Motors Vs. Navin Nishchal & Anr., RP No.
2207 of 2007, decided on 07.08.2012,
this Commission observed:
10. From this, it is clear that reference to an appropriate laboratory (or, expert) for
determination of defects in goods is not entirely mandatory. In this case, based on the
admitted evidence that the complainant was required to take his newly purchased car to
the workshops of the opposite parties repeatedly practically every month the District Forum
specifically observed- Ld. Counsel for the OP submitted that there is no expert opinion that
there is manufacturing defect in the vehicle. In our view no expert opinion is required in the
circumstances of the case as noted above. The vehicle did not run smoothly even for a
month and within two months of the purchase it was taken to the workshop of the OPs with
complaints of high consumption oil and in less than four months started emitting excessive
smoke. The car had to be taken to the workshop of the OPs almost every month with one
problem or the other and one problem, which continued persisting is high consumption of
engine oil and emission of smoke impels us to the inference that there is some
manufacturing defect which is beyond rectification.
In Skoda Auto Volkswagen India (P) Ltd. Vs. Meghna Corporate Ltd., RP No. 589 of
2020 decided on 24.06.2020 (2020) SCC OnLine NCDRC 910), this Commission
observed:
"10. It is argued that there is no compliance by the District Forum of
Section 13(1)(c)
of
Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
Section 13(1)(c)
is reproduced as under:
13. Procedure on admission of complaint. -- (1) The District Forum shall, on admission of
a complaint, if it relates to any goods,--
(a) xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
(b) xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
(c) where the complaint alleges a detect in the goods which cannot be determined without
proper analysis or test of the goods, the District Forum shall obtain a sample of the goods
 from the complainant, seal it and authenticate it m the manner prescribed and refer the
 sample so sealed to the appropriate laboratory along with a direction that such laboratory
 make an analysis or test, whichever may be necessary, with a view to finding out whether
 such goods suffer from any defect alleged in the complaint or from any other defect and to
 report its findings thereon to the District Forum within a period of forty-five days of the
 receipt of the reference or within such extended period as may be granted by the District
 Forum.
11. From the bare reading of this provision, it is apparent that the District Forum is required
 to obtain the expert opinion only when it is of the opinion that the defects as
 mentioned in the Complaint could not be ascertained without proper analysis or test
 of the goods. In the present case, there were 25 job cards showing the repair and
 replacement of various parts of the car, which were based on evidences on record filed
 by the Complainant along with its Complaint and were sufficient for the District Forum to
 determine the nature of the defects in the vehicle. The Petitioner after receiving the notice
 of the Complaint wherein the Complainant had alleged that there were defects in the car,
 had the opportunity to move an appropriate application for obtaining the expert opinion to
 contradict the allegations of the Complainant. That opportunity was not seized by the
 Petitioner. In fact, not even a single piece of evidence has been produced by the Petitioner
 to contradict the contentions of the Complainant/Respondent no.1. Non-compliance of
Section 13(1)(c)
of the Act therefore it not fatal to this case. The findings on which the
 Petitioner has relied upon were given on the facts and circumstances of those cases and
 the facts and circumstances of this case are entirely different. It is apparent that within a
 span of 3½ years till the filing of the Complaint, the vehicle which was new had to
 be taken for repairs to the repairing centre of Respondent no.2 for 25 times. This
 itself shows that the goods supplied were defective."
In view of the foregoing, we hold that laboratory test and/or expert opinion to
 determine/establish a defect and/or manufacturing defect in a good/car, as prescribed
 under
Section 13(1)(c)
is not mandatory in each and every case, its requirement is
 case/fact specific. If there is other reliable, cogent and sufficient evidence on record, it is
 not necessary to have a laboratory test report and/or an expert opinion. Hence, in the
 present case, objection of the OPs that no expert opinion has been produced by the
 Complainant, is not valid."
52. Applying the aforesaid principles, we find that in the instant case the Complainant had been

raising the issue of the vehicle's performance indicating persistent malfunctioning. The defect of

leakage from the sunroof even though attempted to be cured does not seem to be finally cured.

The water leakage resulted in affecting the electronic controls. The vehicle therefore remained in

the same condition with the imperfection having been improved on one occasion or the other but
 the defects continued. The deficiency and defect is evident from the facts as brought on record.

The defect in the sunroof and its leakage relates to manufacturing. The services rendered to

remove the defect were deficient that led to considerable problems as a result where of the vehicle

could not start and had to be towed. As narrated, the engineers sent to retrieve and drive the

vehicle to the garage failed and the vehicle had to be tugged to the workshop. Such performance

during the extended warranty period with a very meagre mileage is evidence of defect.
53. The Complainant was therefore entitled to the satisfactory use of the vehicle and is also

entitled to receive any damages if the defects could not be cured and the deficiency continued.
54. The Complainant had purchased a brand new vehicle, even though on certain incentives but

given the standard of the luxury car that was purchased by the Complainant, it was expected that

the vehicle will perform well. It is not the case of the Opposite Parties that the vehicle had been

driven roughly or handled by untrained hands. The vehicle had been put to good use and had

covered a very meager mileage but at the same time it continued to suffer defects. A customer

having purchased a high-end vehicle does expect reasonably good performance and not to visit

the garage with the vehicle time and again. It is for this reason that the Opposite Parties

immediately offered a 65% discount on the repair and labour costs. To maintain their own

reputation, the Opposite Parties therefore having come across the defects did attempt to rectify

the errors but could not successfully do so.
55. We therefore find that the defects continued as narrated and this deficiency to that extent

deserves to be compensated. The dealer had also not been able to cure the defects effectively

given the period of warranty as well as extended warranty. The vehicle is no longer being

manufactured and therefore there is no question of replacement of the vehicle even if the

Complainant was entitled to it. Apart from this, the vehicle has been used by the Complainant

since 2011 being in his possession and its registration is about to terminate in the year 2026. Thus

keeping in view the two years of the life of the vehicle as now left and keeping in view the fact that

there is no option of replacement of the parts or the same model of the vehicle and the costs
 suffered for repairs, we allow the complaint awarding a sum of Rs.10 lakhs as a lump sum amount

to the Complainant for the harassment suffered on account of the continued and persistent defects

that could not be removed resulting in the imperfect functioning of the vehicle. The liability of all

the OP's is joint and several. With the aforesaid directions, the complaint stands disposed of.
